chosen.premise: Tentacruel normally has 80 poisonous tentacles, but older individuals have fewer.
chosen.hook: Tentacruel gets older—and starts losing its tentacles.
chosen.visualIdea: Compare a young Tentacruel labeled 80 tentacles with an older one whose tentacles fade away.
chosen.note: A remarkably Pokémon-specific contradiction: Tentacruel is defined by having 80 tentacles, yet older individuals have fewer. The single Pokédex entry supports it directly, though it gives no rate or explanation for the loss.

candidates.premise: Tentacruel absorbs water through its tentacles, stretches them almost endlessly, and forms a poisonous net.
candidates.hook: Tentacruel drinks water—and turns its body into a trap.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate short tentacles absorbing water, then extending into a wide, enclosing poisonous net.
candidates.note: The research directly connects water absorption, extreme tentacle extension, and a poisonous net. It is a coherent transformation, though several entries describe related steps rather than one complete mechanism.

candidates.premise: Tentacruel can catch up to 80 prey at once, using its 80 freely moving tentacles.
candidates.hook: How many prey can one Tentacruel catch at the same time? Eighty.
candidates.visualIdea: Show 80 tentacles branching outward, each wrapping around a separate fish silhouette.
candidates.note: The 80-prey claim is concrete and highly visual, but the evidence says it can catch up to 80 prey—not necessarily one prey per tentacle—so the tentacle-to-prey implication should be phrased carefully.

candidates.premise: Tentacruel’s red orbs communicate warnings and signal that an ultrasonic attack is about to fire.
candidates.hook: Those red orbs aren’t decoration—they’re Tentacruel’s warning system.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into the red orbs as they blink a warning, then flash brightly before ultrasonic waves erupt.
candidates.note: The evidence clearly supports blinking orbs as communication and bright orbs as a pre-attack signal. Strong screen language, but the premise combines warning communication with ultrasonic weapon activation.

candidates.premise: When a large Tentacruel outbreak occurs, all fish Pokémon disappear from the surrounding sea.
candidates.hook: A Tentacruel outbreak can empty an entire sea of fish Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a crowded sea suddenly emptying as multiple Tentacruel silhouettes spread across it.
candidates.note: A striking ecological consequence backed directly by the Moon entry. It says fish Pokémon disappear during a large outbreak, but does not establish whether Tentacruel eat them, drive them away, or cause the disappearance another way.

candidates.premise: Tentacool evolves into Tentacruel when it reaches level 30.
candidates.hook: At level 30, Tentacool becomes this 80-tentacled hunter.
candidates.visualIdea: Display Tentacool beside Tentacruel, with a level counter climbing to 30 before the evolution.
candidates.note: Very clear and easy to animate, but level-30 evolution is standard Pokémon trivia and is less distinctive or surprising than Tentacruel’s biology. The evolution method is from trusted secondary research rather than a Pokédex entry.

rounds.request: The chosen angle is strong enough. Even stronger research would add a concrete age threshold, a typical tentacle count at different ages, or an explanation for why Tentacruel loses tentacles over time.
